{"filepath": "battery_comparison_research.md", "content": "# Sodium-Ion vs. Lithium-Ion Home Energy Storage Batteries: Comprehensive Research Report (2026)

This research report compares sodium-ion (Na-ion) and lithium-ion (specifically Lithium Iron Phosphate [LFP] and Nickel Manganese Cobalt [NMC]) home energy storage batteries across key metrics: market data, costs, energy density, lifecycle, and safety.

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Market Context

Lithium-ion technology—predominantly Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) for stationary residential storage—has been the gold standard for residential solar-plus-storage systems. However, sodium-ion technology has emerged as a viable alternative, gaining commercial momentum through manufacturers like CATL, BYD, and emerging energy storage suppliers. 

While sodium-ion benefits from the earth's abundance and cheap raw materials (salt), early-stage manufacturing scale means current cell-level and system-level costs are roughly comparable to or slightly higher than mature LFP chemistries, though projected long-term scaling suggests significant cost advantages.

---

## 2. Technical Metrics Comparison

| Metric / Parameter | Sodium-Ion (Na-ion) | Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) | NMC Lithium-Ion |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gravimetric Energy Density** | 100 – 175 Wh/kg | 120 – 200 Wh/kg | 200 – 250 Wh/kg |
| **Cell Cost (2025/2026 Est.)** | $80 – $120 / kWh | $100 – $150 / kWh | $130 – $180 / kWh |
| **Cycle Life (Manufacturer Claims)** | 3,000 – 6,000 cycles | 4,000 – 6,000+ cycles | 3,000 – 5,000 cycles |
| **Low-Temperature Performance** | Excellent (>90% retention at -20°C) | Moderate (70–75% retention at -20°C) | Good (>85% retention at -20°C) |
| **Transport & Storage State** | Can be shipped at 0V (safe logistics) | Must be shipped at partial state-of-charge | Must be shipped at partial state-of-charge |

---

## 3. Detailed Breakdown of Key Metrics

### A. Costs and Market Pricing
* **Cell Costs:** Sodium-ion cell production is projected at $80–$120/kWh, whereas LFP cells range from $100–$150/kWh and NMC cells range from $130–$180/kWh.
* **System-Level Pricing:** Because sodium-ion supply chains are still scaling up for residential applications, system-level integration (inverters, BMS, housing) often matches or exceeds mature LFP home battery systems (such as Tesla Powerwall or equivalent LFP stacks), with home storage system pricing hovering around $500–$600/kWh.

### B. Energy Density & Form Factor
* **Volumetric and Gravimetric Trade-offs:** LFP packs deliver 160–200 Wh/kg, whereas sodium-ion sits slightly lower at 110–175 Wh/kg. 
* **Home Impact:** For stationary home storage where physical footprint is less constrained than in electric vehicles, the slight difference in energy density is manageable, though sodium-ion battery cabinets may require marginally more physical wall or floor space for the same kWh capacity.

### C. Lifecycle and Durability
* **Cycle Life:** Leading LFP cells reliably achieve 6,000+ cycles, making them exceptionally durable for daily cycling over 10–15+ years. Sodium-ion currently demonstrates 3,000 to 6,000 cycles depending on the specific cathode/anode formulation, catching up fast but trailing top-tier LFP in longevity.
* **Low-Temperature Resilience:** Sodium-ion excels in extreme cold, retaining over 90% of its capacity at -20°C compared to 70–75% for LFP, making sodium-ion exceptionally attractive for unheated garages or cold-climate installations.

### D. Safety and Thermal Stability
* **Thermal Runaway Onset:** Sodium-ion batteries possess higher thermal runaway initiation temperatures (often 220°C to 260°C) compared to LFP (170°C to 220°C) and significantly higher than NMC (~150°C).
* **Heat Release & Off-Gases:** Nail penetration and crush tests indicate sodium-ion cells generate peak temperature rises 40°C–60°C lower than lithium cells and emit fewer toxic off-gases (such as reduced hydrogen fluoride risks associated with certain lithium salts).
* **Logistics:** Sodium-ion cells can be safely discharged to 0V for transport and storage, virtually eliminating fire risks during shipping and initial installation.

---

## 4. Sources & Citations

2. **Bonnen Batteries:** [Sodium-Ion vs Lithium-Ion Battery: 2026 Comparison](https://www.bonnenbatteries.com/bonnen-batteries/sodium-ion-battery-vs-lithium-ion-battery-a-friendly-comparison) — Analyzed raw material abundance, current production scale economics, and cost parity trends.
3. **Kora Power:** [LFP vs. Sodium-Ion Home Battery: Why LFP Wins in 2026](https://korapower.com/blogs/education/lfp-vs-sodium-ion-home-battery-2026-homeowners-guide) — Compared practical residential constraints, cycle life (3,000–5,000 vs 6,000+), and gravimetric energy density.
4. **Zvepow Safety Analysis:** [Sodium Ion vs LFP Battery for Energy Storage: 2026 Comparison](https://www.zvepow.com/news/sodium-ion-vs-lfp-battery) — Sourced thermal runaway onset temperatures, nail penetration data, and fire suppression system cost impacts.
5. **Sunlit Energy:** [Sodium-Ion Battery Safety vs Lithium-Ion (2026)](https://sunlithenergy.com/sunlit-energy/sodium-ion-battery-safety-vs-lithium-ion) — Examined crystallization breakdown temperatures and oxygen-fed fire risks.
6. **ESS News:** [Comparing safety profiles of lithium-ion, sodium-ion and solid-state batteries](https://www.ess-news.com/2026/02/11/comparing-safety-profiles-of-lithium-ion-sodium-ion-and-solid-state-batteries) — Referenced off-gas composition, hydrogen content comparisons, and 0V transport safety advantages.
